answer: An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the tide check immediately, the plume audit keeps the resolved set and the cipher replay makes public exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 210 aliases hence pays the reading cost 210 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
